claim_ceiling: At the resolution of the source-bound official Yale image, the f68r2.31 ending remains an ambiguous continuation of the circular register rather than an independently readable plain-script anchor. No SUN/Suna word, koiin preference, sound, language, cipher, plaintext, meaning, or translation is established.

visual_observations.observation: The lower face medallion is surrounded by one continuous circular text register, and most of that register consists of ordinary Voynich-style forms.
The disputed ending occupies the same narrow circular band and follows the ordinary ring text; it is not drawn as a separate caption or inscription.
The disputed marks share the local brown visual tone and approximate writing scale, but are appreciably fainter and more irregular than the clearest neighboring forms.
Magnified views at four orientations do not yield a stable four-letter plain-script segmentation or a sequence that can be read independently of a proposed word.
The official image does not independently support the reading SUN or Suna.
The image does not decide between the ZL3b/RF1b treatment as four illegible marks and IT2a's ordinary koiin ending.
The ordinary-light image cannot determine whether weak visibility is caused chiefly by faded or abraded ink, parchment texture, local paint interference, or atypical letterforms.
